'''Edward Taylor Pegg Jr.''' (born December 7, 1963) is an expert on mathematical [[puzzle]]s and is a self-described [[Recreational mathematics|recreational]] [[mathematician]]. He wrote an online puzzle column called Ed Pegg Jr.'s ''Math Games'' for the [[Mathematical Association of America]] during the years 2003–2007. His puzzles have also been used by [[Will Shortz]] on the puzzle segment of [[National Public Radio|NPR's]] ''[[Weekend Edition|Weekend Edition Sunday]]''. He was a fan of [[Martin Gardner]] and regularly participated in [[Gathering 4 Gardner]] conferences. In 2009, he teamed up with [[Tom Malin Rodgers|Tom M. Rodgers]] and [[Alan Schoen]] to edit two Gardner tribute books.<ref>''Homage to a Pied Puzzler'' (AK Peters) {{ISBN | 9781336100640}}; ''Mathematical Wizardry for a Gardner'' (AK Peters) {{ISBN | 9781336100381}}</ref>

Pegg received a master's degree in mathematics from the [[University of Colorado Colorado Springs|University of Colorado at Colorado Springs]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://education.wolfram.com/summer/school/faculty/2005/|title=Wolfram Summer School 2005 Faculty}}</ref> writing his thesis on the subject of fair dice.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Pegg|first=Edward Taylor Jr.|title=A complete list of fair dice|year=1994}}</ref> In 2000, he left [[NORAD]] to join [[Wolfram Research]], where he collaborated on ''[[A New Kind of Science]]'' (NKS). In 2004, he started assisting [[Eric W. Weisstein]] at Wolfram [[MathWorld]].<ref>[http://mathworld.wolfram.com/news/2004-10-11/mathworld-tshirt/#pegg MathWorld Headline News] and [http://mathworld.wolfram.com/about/ About MathWorld]. Retrieved on January 31, 2007.</ref> He has made contributions to several hundred MathWorld articles.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weisstein |first=Eric W. |title=Pegg -- from Wolfram MathWorld |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/ |access-date=2023-12-21 |website=mathworld.wolfram.com |language=en}}</ref> He was one of the chief consultants for ''[[Numb3rs]]''.
